staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this exact vulnerable tmux checkout. The packaged `patch.diff` contains several unrelated hunks, but the relevant fix for this sample is the `regsub.c` change that adds `cp[1] != '\0'` before consuming a backslash escape.

bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in regsub OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=499446092 `Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: regsub format_replace format_expand1`
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in the staged vulnerable tmux checkout while `cmd-parse-fuzzer` parsed the saved 48-byte witness. The saved crash summary closes the downstream chain `regsub_expand -> regsub -> format_replace -> format_expand1`, and the fixing hunk proves the missing obligation: vulnerable `regsub_expand()` treats a final `'\\'` in the substitution replacement string as the start of an escape even when no following byte exists. That advances `cp` onto the terminating NUL, the `for` loop increment advances it once more past the heap buffer, and the next loop-condition read dereferences one byte out of bounds. For this exact witness, Stage 02 does not claim a statically closed `%if` or lexer-admission story because the raw bytes contain `0xff` between `%if` and `#{`; the trace is therefore anchored at the first downstream project statement whose reachability is closed by the saved crash artifacts and the staged vulnerable source.

parser_admitted.description: The fuzz input has passed `cmd_parse_do_buffer()` and is admitted into tmux command construction; rejected command-parser inputs return before this accepted continuation.

admitted_location.description: A parsed command has successfully built a command list entry and is appended to the current command list before the downstream format expansion path is reached.

source.description: Source. `format_replace()` materializes the attacker-derived format key that reached the crashing path into mutable heap string `copy` before parsing modifiers.
source.value_from: The earlier raw-byte transition from the `%if\xff...` witness into this `key,keylen` pair is not statically closed for this exact sample. The saved crash summary and local source semantics do close the chain from this statement forward.

sink.description: ASan sink. After escape handling has already moved `cp` onto the terminator and the loop increment has advanced it once more, the next loop test dereferences `*cp` one byte past the heap buffer that holds the replacement string.
sink.note: The saved ASan report says the invalid read is at `0x506000000360`, exactly 0 bytes after a 64-byte heap region. That matches the initial `len = 64; buf = xmalloc(len);` allocation in `format_expand1()` for the replacement string buffer later passed as `with` to `regsub()`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `regsub_expand()` consumes a backslash escape even when the backslash is the final character in `with`, so it advances `cp` onto the terminator without checking that a following byte exists.
root_cause.note: The fixing hunk changes this exact branch to `if (cp[0] == '\\' && cp[1] != '\0')`, proving the missing trailing-backslash guard is the violated obligation on the crashing path.

tainted_value_origin.code:
right = format_expand1(es, sub[i]->argv[1]);
new = format_sub(sub[i], value, left, right);
tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the stored replacement operand for the substitution modifier becomes the concrete heap string `right` and is immediately passed toward `regsub()` as `with`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The exact raw witness bytes that produced `sub[i]->argv[1]` are not reconstructed here. But the saved crash plus the `regsub.c` fix close the downstream fact that the concrete `right` string reaching `regsub_expand()` ended in a lone trailing backslash.

evidence_limitations: The saved witness bytes are `25 69 66 ff 23 7b ...`, so there is a raw `0xff` byte between `%if` and `#{`. From the staged vulnerable source alone, Stage 02 does not statically close how that exact byte sequence is tokenized into the `format_replace(key,keylen)` input that later crashes. The GT therefore avoids `yylex_format()` and `%if #{...}` claims and anchors at the first downstream statement closed by the crash summary and local source flow.

The saved `sanitizer_trace.txt` is unsymbolized. Exact line attribution inside the `regsub` stack is inferred from the saved crash summary (`regsub -> format_replace -> format_expand1`), the vulnerable source, the 64-byte ASan allocation size, the `reproduction_report.json` summary naming `regsub_expand`, and the one-line fixing hunk in `patch.diff`, not from a symbolized PC-to-line map.

Stage 02 stayed source-grounded and did not rerun a fixed build, rebuild the project, or add instrumentation. The PoC contract below is limited to the exact saved 48-byte witness and the closed downstream substitution path proved from `format_replace()` into `regsub_expand()`.

coarse_trace.summary: Once attacker-derived format text reaches `format_replace()`, tmux copies it, parses modifiers from the copied key, and retains an `s` substitution modifier with at least two arguments for later execution.
The replacement operand of that stored substitution modifier is re-expanded into a heap buffer and passed into `regsub()` as the replacement string `with`.

A lone trailing backslash in `with` takes the escape branch in `regsub_expand()`, moves the cursor onto the terminator, then the loop increment moves it past the allocation and the next loop test performs the saved out-of-bounds read.

fine_trace.note: Source. `format_replace()` copies the attacker-derived format key that reached the crashing path into heap string `copy`, creating the mutable parser state used for modifier parsing.
While parsing wrapped modifier arguments from `copy`, tmux materializes each argument as its own heap string and stores it in the modifier's `argv[]` array.

fine_trace.code:
sub = xreallocarray(sub, nsub + 1, sizeof *sub);
sub[nsub++] = fm;
fine_trace.note: When the parsed modifier is `s` and has at least two arguments, tmux retains it in the `sub[]` list so its replacement operand will be executed later rather than discarded.
Re-expanding the stored replacement operand starts with a 64-byte heap buffer. The saved ASan allocation context matches this exact default extent.

fine_trace.code:
right = format_expand1(es, sub[i]->argv[1]);
new = format_sub(sub[i], value, left, right);
fine_trace.note: When substitution is applied, tmux re-expands the stored replacement operand into heap string `right` and immediately passes it into `format_sub()`. The downstream crash and fix imply that this concrete `right` string ends with a lone trailing backslash.
The replacement string `right` becomes `with` at the `regsub()` call boundary, carrying the trailing-backslash condition into `regsub_expand()`.

Root cause. On the final character of `with`, vulnerable `regsub_expand()` treats the lone trailing backslash as an escape introducer and advances `cp` onto the terminating NUL even though no escaped byte follows.
After step 7 falls through, the `for` loop increment executes and advances `cp` one byte past the string terminator, so the cursor is now outside the allocated replacement buffer.
Sink. The next loop-condition evaluation dereferences `*cp` after `cp` has already moved past the 64-byte heap buffer, producing the saved `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `regsub_expand`.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan report says the invalid read happens exactly 0 bytes after a 64-byte heap region. `format_expand1()` allocates that default 64-byte buffer immediately before the replacement string is passed into `regsub()`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The relevant `regsub.c` hunk in the staged `patch.diff` changes the vulnerable branch from `if (*cp == '\\') {` to `if (cp[0] == '\\' && cp[1] != '\0') {`, which prevents a lone trailing backslash from advancing the cursor onto the terminator and then past the end of the replacement buffer.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The patch guards the exact branch that converts a trailing backslash in `with` into an out-of-bounds loop advance, and the ASan 64-byte region size matches the replacement buffer allocated by `format_expand1()` immediately before `regsub()`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Closed from `format_replace()` onward. The earlier `%if 0xff ...` raw-byte tokenization into `format_replace(key,keylen)` is left as an explicit evidence limitation rather than asserted.

format.name: raw cmd-parse-fuzzer byte buffer
format.contract: Exactly the saved 48-byte witness `25 69 66 ff 23 7b 64 3b 73 23 58 23 5c 23 fd 20 69 3b 6c 3b 73 73 69 7b 6f 16 69 6e 70 75 74 64 2d 3a 3a 1a 1a 3e c3 8f 83 07 a2 c5 23 5c 58 7d`. Stage 02 does not generalize this into a wider accepted-input class and does not claim a statically closed parser explanation for the `0xff` byte between `%if` and `#{`; it only claims the downstream path proved by the saved crash and staged source, namely that this witness reaches `format_replace()` and then `regsub_expand()` with a replacement string whose final character is a lone backslash.
